verses.74:2: {confit2}, Deus: * daremos graças, e invocaremos o vosso nome.
verses.74:4: {liquefacta} a terra, e todos os que nela habitam: * eu {confirmavi} as suas colunas.
verses.74:5: Eu disse aos iníquos: {iniqueagere}: * e aos que cometem faltas: Não {exaltare5} o chifre:
verses.74:6: Não ergais {inaltum} o vosso chifre: * não {loqui} iniquidade contra Deus.
verses.74:7: {quia} nem do oriente, nem do ocidente, nem {desertis}: * {quoniam} Deus é juiz.
verses.74:9: {inclinavit} {exhoc}: todavia, a sua borra {exinanita}: * beberão todos os pecadores da terra.
verses.74:10: {egoautem} anunciarei para sempre: * cantarei ao Deus de Jacó.
verses.74:11: E quebrarei todos os chifres dos pecadores: * e {exaltare11} os chifres do justo.

decisions.why: *confitéri* to God → *dar graças a* (D5). The first *confitébimur* has *tibi*, the second has none, as the Latin (43:9 *daremos graças* without a pronoun). The dative pronoun needs a place in Portuguese: proclisis wants a word before it, so the subject *Nós* is named (a subject hidden in the verb ending, rule 2). The mesóclise *Dar-vos-emos graças* is correct but stiff at the head of a psalm.

options.label: Nós vos daremos graças
options.note: Ruling: D5; subject named for the proclitic *vos*; MS1932 *Nós te louvaremos* has the same build.

options.label: Dar-vos-emos graças
options.note: mesóclise; opens on the verb as the Latin does, but reads as written Portuguese.

decisions.why: The speaker changes: *narrábimus* is 'we', *accépero … judicábo* is 'I', and the Greek (λάβω καιρόν) and most readers take the 'I' as God; the Latin does not say so, and neither does the Portuguese. *accípere tempus* is 'take / receive a time' (L&S accipio: take, receive; καιρός is the fit moment); DRB 'when I shall take a time'; MS1932 turns it *No tempo que eu tiver fixado* (fixing is not in the word). *tomar o tempo* keeps the verb; its risk is being heard as 'take up time'. *eu* named because *tomar* (future subjunctive) is also third person, and the ear must not hear 'when he takes'. The future perfect *accépero* is said, as usual, by the future subjunctive. v2: the stylist found *eu … eu* heavy in one short colon (the Latin names *ego* once, at *judicábo*); the first *eu* is dropped — the person of *tomar* is fixed by *eu julgarei* in the same breath. The ambiguity reader heard *tomar o tempo* first as 'find the time'; it is close to the Latin's own 'take a time', and kept. Glossary: the *accípere* row has *receber* (23:4–5, 49:9); here *tomar* (17:17's verb) is a local departure, because the one who speaks takes the time rather than being given it (λάβω); recorded in the row.

options.label: quando tomar o tempo
options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist's; *ego* said once, at the verb it stands beside.

options.label: quando eu tiver tomado o tempo

forms.tempus: quando eu tiver tomado o tempo

options.note: the future perfect to the letter.

options.label: no tempo que eu tiver fixado

forms.tempus: no tempo que eu tiver fixado

decisions.why: The *justítiæ* (plural) row keeps the Latin's plural (*as justiças*: 10:8, 17:23, 18:9, 49:16) and names 74:3 as a place to decide locally. The Greek here is εὐθύτητας ('uprightnesses'), an internal object: 'I will judge upright judgements', i.e. judge uprightly; DRB keeps the plural object ('I will judge justices'); MS1932 *julgarei com justiça*. Kept as the row: an object the Latin gives, with the Latin's plural; *ego* said as *eu* (it is emphatic in the Latin). Risk: *as justiças* heard as 'the courts' — the ambiguity reader is asked. *com justiça* and *retamente* (57:2 *recta judicáte → julgai retamente*) are one touch away.

options.label: eu julgarei com justiça
options.note: MS1932; the object becomes manner, the plural lost.

options.label: eu julgarei retamente
options.note: the Greek's εὐθύτητας; 57:2's adverb; loses the word *justiça*.

decisions.why: *liquefácere* passive, ἐτάκη 'melted'. *derreter-se* is the melting of wax at 21:15b (*cera que se derrete*), and keeps the image concrete (rule 5). MS1932 *dissolveu-se* is more abstract. The pronominal form for the Latin passive, verb first as the Latin.

The *confirmáre* row (open) proposes *confirmar* only where a word is confirmed, *firmar* where a thing is set fast (37:3 *firmastes … a vossa mão*) or a person is the object. Pillars are set fast: *confirmei as suas colunas* would be heard as 'I verified its pillars'. ἐστερέωσα, 'made firm'. MS1932 *fortaleci*.

options.label: firmei
options.note: Ruling: the row's *firmar* for a thing set fast.

decisions.why: The Latin echoes itself, *iníquis … iníque* (the Greek too: παρανομοῦσιν μὴ παρανομεῖτε), and the echo is kept: *aos iníquos: Não ajais iniquamente*. The *iníqua ágere* row gives *agir iniquamente* (open; a blind reader once listed *iniquamente* as unknown); *praticar a iniquidade* is operári's and is refused for that reason. *Nolíte* + infinitive is the plain negative imperative in Portuguese (*Não ajais*); 'do not will to' is not said. *ajais* is a rare form but a regular one. v2: the ambiguity reader listed *ajais* and *iniquamente* as unknown; kept for the echo *iníquos … iniquamente* (no remark from the Latinist or the stylist). *Não procedais* is one touch away.

options.label: Não ajais iniquamente
options.note: Ruling: the row; keeps the echo.

options.label: Não procedais iniquamente
options.note: avoids *ajais*; *proceder* is not the Latin's plainest verb.

options.label: Não pratiqueis a maldade
options.note: MS1932 *Não pratiqueis mais a maldade*; loses the echo and spends operári's verb.

decisions.latin: Nolíte exaltáre cornu … et exaltabúntur córnua justi
decisions.why: *exaltáre → exaltar* (row, working), and here the psalm is built on it: the sinners are told not to exalt the horn (74:5), and at the end the horns of the just shall be exalted (74:11); 74:8 *hunc exáltat* sits between. One verb three times keeps the frame. *cornu → chifre* (row; *corno* is an insult in Brazil). DRB 'lift up'; MS1932 turns the horn into *a vossa fronte soberba* and *a fronte do justo*, which paraphrases the image (refused, rule 5).

options.label: exalteis / serão exaltados
options.note: Ruling: the row; the psalm's frame.

options.label: levanteis / serão levantados
options.note: DRB 'lift up'; *levantar* is leváre's in the glossary, and breaks the echo with 74:8.

decisions.latin: Nolíte extóllere in altum cornu vestrum
decisions.why: *extóllere → erguer* (row; 27:2, 27:9; the row names 74:6). *in altum* (εἰς ὕψος), 'on high': *para o alto* is the plain direction; *ao alto* is shorter but is heard as a command ('Ao alto!').

decisions.latin: Quia neque ab Oriénte … quóniam Deus judex est
decisions.why: The verse is an anacoluthon: 'for neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert mountains —' and the thing that does not come from there is never named (the Hebrew: 'lifting up'); then *quóniam Deus judex est*. The Portuguese leaves the gap where the Latin leaves it (MS1932's parenthesis *vos virá auxílio* is a gloss, not text). *Quia … quóniam* are both *porque* by the defaults; said twice, the second *porque* is heard as taking up the first, which is what the Latin does. v2: the stylist heard *porque … porque* at the head of both cola as a stutter, and the Latin itself varies the word (*quia / quóniam*); the second becomes *pois*.

options.label: Porque … pois
options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist's; varies where the Latin varies.

decisions.why: *desértus* is an adjective of the mountains ('desert, desolate hills', ἐρήμων ὀρέων; DRB 'desert hills'; MS1932 *pelos montes desertos*). The Hebrew has 'the desert of the mountains' — not followed. *desertos* in Portuguese is 'deserted / waste', the Latin adjective's own sense.

decisions.latin: Hunc humíliat, et hunc exáltat … ex hoc in hoc
decisions.why: *hic … hic* is the Latin's idiom for 'this one … that one' (τοῦτον … τοῦτον; DRB 'One … another'). Portuguese *a este … a este* is not the idiom and can be heard as one man humbled and exalted; *este … aquele* is (MS1932 *A este humilha, e àquele exalta*), and keeps a demonstrative in both places. 74:9 *ex hoc in hoc* is the same pair, so it follows in the same slot: *deste para aquele*. The literal repetition is option 2.

options.label: a este … àquele / deste para aquele

forms.hunc: A este humilha, e àquele exalta

options.label: a este … a este / deste para este

forms.hunc: A este humilha, e a este exalta

options.note: the Latin's repetition to the letter.

options.label: a um … a outro / de um para outro

forms.hunc: A um humilha, e a outro exalta

decisions.latin: quia calix in manu Dómini vini meri plenus misto
decisions.why: Verbless; *há* supplied (rule 2). *calix → cálice* (row). *merum* is unmixed wine (*vinho puro*), and the cup of unmixed wine is *plenus misto*, 'full of mixture' (πλῆρες κεράσματος; DRB 'a cup of strong wine full of mixture'): the Latin's paradox — pure wine, full of a mixture (spices, a drugged draught) — is kept as the Latin leaves it, unexplained. *cálice* is a proparoxytone and here does not stand at a cadence. The colon runs some five syllables over the Latin.

options.label: na mão do Senhor há um cálice de vinho puro, cheio de mistura

forms.calix: na mão do Senhor há um cálice de vinho puro, cheio de mistura

options.note: Ruling; MS1932 builds the verse the same way (*há um cálice que contém vinho puro cheio de mistura*).

options.label: há na mão do Senhor um cálice de vinho puro, cheio de mistura

forms.calix: há na mão do Senhor um cálice de vinho puro, cheio de mistura

options.note: the Latin's order: the cup before the hand.

decisions.latin: Et inclinávit ex hoc in hoc
decisions.why: *inclinávit* has no object in the Latin; the thing tilted is the cup of 74:8. Portuguese *inclinou deste para aquele* with no object dangles; the pronoun *o* is grammar and names nothing the Latin does not imply. The subject (the Lord) is the Latin's hidden one. v2: the Latinist (minor) asked for the bare *E inclinou*, calling the supplied *o* defensible. Refused: without an object Portuguese *inclinou deste para aquele* is heard as intransitive, 'he leaned from this one to that' — a new sense; the pronoun is grammar (rule 2) and the ambiguity reader heard it as the cup.

decisions.latin: verúmtamen fæx ejus non est exinaníta
decisions.why: *verúmtamen → todavia* (row). *fæx → borra* (D41). *exinaníre* is 'empty out' (ἐξεκενώθη); of dregs Portuguese says *esgotar-se* ('be drained'), MS1932 *não se esgotaram*; *esvaziar* is the root sense but a sediment is not 'emptied'. *ejus*: the cup's; *a sua* is left to point back to it. v2: the Latinist (minor) asked for the passive *não foi esvaziada*: the Latin is a passive perfect. The voice is taken, the verb kept: *não foi esgotada* — dregs are drained, not 'emptied'.

options.label: não foi esgotada
options.note: Ruling (v2): the Latin's passive (Latinist), MS1932's verb.

options.label: não foi esvaziada
options.note: the Latinist's fix; the root sense of *exinaníre*.

decisions.why: The *ego autem* row allows *mas eu* or *eu, porém*. 58:17 *Ego autem cantábo* is *Eu, porém, cantarei*, and this verse is the same turn (and ends *cantábo*): *Eu, porém,* kept for the echo. *annuntiáre → anunciar* (D41), with no object, as the Latin (MS1932 adds *estas coisas*). The Greek has ἀγαλλιάσομαι 'I will rejoice' where the Latin reads *annuntiábo*; the Latin is followed.

*loqui* with a content object → *falar* + noun (the *loqui mendácium* row: *falar mentira*, 16:9b *falou soberba*, 57:2 *falais justiça*). The stylist heard *falar iniquidade* as a calque and asked *digais*; refused — *dícere* is *dizer* in this psalm (74:5 *Dixi → Eu disse*) and the row keeps the content object with *falar*. His line is option 2.

choices.74:2: *invocáre → invocar* (row); *nomen tuum → o vosso nome*. The repeated *confitébimur* is repeated.
choices.74:3: *narráre → narrar*, *mirabília → maravilhas* (9:2, 25:7). The switch from 'we' to 'I' is the Latin's and is not smoothed.
choices.74:4: *omnes qui hábitant in ea → todos os que nela habitam*. *ego → eu*, emphatic as the Latin.
choices.74:5: *Dixi → Eu disse* (38:2). *delinquéntibus → aos que cometem faltas* (row *delínquere*, 24:8). The colon ends on ':' as the Latin, which runs on into 74:6. *cornu* has no possessive here (74:6 adds *vestrum*), so *o chifre*.
choices.74:6: *loqui iniquitátem* → *falar iniquidade*: the content object kept (the *loqui mendácium* row; 57:2 *falais justiça*); *contra Deus* moved after the object, natural order.
choices.74:7: *judex → juiz*; *Deus judex est → Deus é juiz*, no article, as 49:6.
choices.74:9: The Latin's inner ':' without a mark is kept. *bibent* has no object; none is supplied (MS1932 adds *delas*). *peccatóres terræ → os pecadores da terra*.
choices.74:10: *cantáre → cantar*: the Latin has *cantábo* where the Greek has ψαλῶ; the Latin's verb is followed, so not *entoarei salmos* (D25). *Deo Jacob → ao Deus de Jacó* (19:2, 23:6, 45:8).
choices.74:11: *confríngere → quebrar* (row). Object first in the Latin; natural order in Portuguese. *justi* singular kept: *do justo*.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from parallels (no Diurnal text for this psalm in the parallels file). Hard readings: 74:3 *cum accépero tempus* and the speaker's change; *justítias judicábo* (plural internal object); 74:7's anacoluthon, left open; 74:8 *vini meri plenus misto*, the paradox kept; *hic … hic* as 'this … that'.

Hard checks pass. Soft: 74:5a +3 (the echo *iníquos … iniquamente* costs syllables; accepted), 74:6b −4 (Portuguese is shorter; accepted), 74:7a −4 (accepted), 74:8a +3 (*àquele* for the idiom), 74:8b +5 (the supplied *há* and the articles; within one breath), 74:9a/b +3 (accepted). No rhyme flags.
